cover.title: Rotated arrays
cover.lead: Sorted, then cut once. Compare the middle with the last value to find the drop.
cover.use_it_when: The array rises, drops once, then rises again, and you need the minimum or a target.
cover.why_it_matters: It shows binary search needs a yes/no question, not a fully sorted array.

final.caption: low meets high at slot {{MIN_AT}}: the minimum is {{MIN}}.

slides.title: A cut deck
slides.scene: A sorted deck of cards is cut once: the top part goes to the bottom. Now it rises, drops once, and rises again.

blocks.label: THE SMALLEST CARD SITS AT THE DROP

blocks.text: Find the drop and you have the smallest card. You don't need to look at every card.

slides.title: Check the last value
slides.lead: Values before the drop beat the last one.

blocks.text: **6** > [[3]] → the drop is right of the middle

quickcheck.question: 6 7 1 2 3 4 5: which slot holds its minimum?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: slot {{find_min_index([6, 7, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5])}}, the 1. The drop comes after 7.

blocks.label: FIND 2 IN 4 5 6 1 2 3
blocks.note: 4 ≤ 6, so slots 0 to 2 are sorted. 2 isn't between 4 and 6, so search the right half.

blocks.text: Any middle splits the array into two halves, and at least one of them is sorted. Check if the target fits inside the sorted one. That's LeetCode 33.

slides.title: Find the minimum
slides.explain: Line 7: the drop is right of the middle. Line 9: the middle may be the minimum, so keep it.

slides.title: Use high, not low
slides.lead: Compare with nums[low] and the drop can hide.

right.note: The last value always sits after the drop.

cost.note: Needs distinct values, as in LeetCode 153.

blog.summary: In a sorted array cut once, compare the middle with the last value to know which side the drop is on.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (one value, two values both ways, the LeetCode 153 examples, no rotation, rotation by one at each end, values at the problem's limits), one rotated array of 5,000 values, and random rotated arrays of up to 15 distinct values
blog.tested_extra: The steps in the walk-through, the quick-check slot and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: Binary search on a rotated sorted array: find the minimum by comparing the middle with the last value (LeetCode 153 and 33).
lines: Before the drop every value is bigger than the last one, after it none is. One compare picks the side.
The trap: compare with nums[low] instead and 4 5 6 1 2 3 returns {{wrong_find_min(EXAMPLE)}}, not {{MIN}}.
